result:
I graded Riley's second attempt at quiz 0001: three items correct, two partial, one wrong. The grades are in `grades/0001-s2.json`.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback in brief |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model outputs a request that names the tool and its arguments. This is better than the first attempt. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | A stuck loop needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. Riley had this right on the first attempt. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | The count of 4 is right, but the reason is wrong. The program runs the tools, not the model. |
| q5 | correct | The result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide its next step. |
| q6 | partial | The name is only part of it. The model relies on the whole tool description: name, purpose and parameters. |

**Summary:** Riley has the core of the loop. Two ideas need fixing. The program runs the tools, never the model, so each step is a separate model call. A loop also needs a stopping condition, because repeating will not fix a stuck agent.

**Next step:** write the tool description for `check_calendar`, with its name, purpose and parameters, and explain how the model would use it. Then redo q3 and q4 from memory in a few days.

I also wrote `learning-records/0003-quiz-0001-second-attempt.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. I didn't grade `s1`, since you only asked for `s2`.
